Fine, Arkady Borisovich, we are waiting for you here.
I will quickly grab all necessary documents right now.
The car is already parked downstairs in the courtyard.
Is the driver ready to head toward the airport?

I need to think calmly before the long journey.
Do not worry, our flight departs strictly on time.
I am finally completely free from house arrest.
I congratulate you on the long-awaited city court decision.
Thank you, now a new life begins for us.
We are ready to reliably protect you everywhere.

meanings.note: Домашний арест = house arrest. Borrowed via German 'Arrest' from Medieval Latin 'arrestum' (stoppage, seizure).

examples.trans: The court has decided: house arrest at his registered address.

meanings.note: В аэропорту = at the airport. Common masculine noun meaning 'airport' in everyday Russian.

examples.trans: We are driving to the airport.
Are you joking? Put on the airport!

meanings.note: Compartment of a car for luggage. Derived noun with agent/object suffix '-ник'/'-щик'/'-чик'. Common masculine noun meaning 'trunk, boot, luggage rack' in everyday Russian.

examples.trans: Yes, all things have already been loaded into the trunk.

meanings.en: on time, at the right moment
meanings.note: 'не вовремя' = at a bad moment. Prefix 'во-' ('into, up') marks inward or upward movement (stem 'время').

meanings.note: трезвый водитель = designated / sober driver service

meanings.note: To depart by plane or fly out. Prefix 'вы-' ('out of') marks outward movement or thorough completion (stem 'летать'). Used as an imperfective (ongoing/repeated action) verb meaning 'to depart, to fly out', paired with 'вылететь'.

examples.trans: The plane departs in an hour.

examples.text: Наш частный самолёт вылетает через три часа.

выходить.gloss: to go out, to get out

meanings.note: Relating to a город. Relational adjective formed with the Slavic suffix '-ский' ('pertaining to'). Agrees in gender, number, and case with the noun it modifies ('city, town, municipal').

meanings.note: Подожди! = wait!. Prefix 'под-' ('under, up to') indicates approaching or supporting from below (stem 'ождать'). Used as an perfective (single completed action) verb meaning 'to wait (a while)', paired with 'ждать'.

meanings.note: Поздравляю! = congratulations!. Prefix 'по-' forms perfective verbs or marks a brief/onset action (stem 'здравлять'). Used as an imperfective (ongoing/repeated action) verb meaning 'to congratulate', paired with 'поздравить'.
